recap.workouts:
One session on the calendar today and it did not get past the warm-up.

CFF16 — started 07:34, stopped at 5:09. 2.72 km, load 3 against a planned 131, and intervals.icu never paired it to the planned session, which is what an early stop normally does. No gym today and none prescribed. Nothing came through on the phone either, so tonight is read off the file rather than off your words.

What the five minutes show, since that is all there is. Power ramped smoothly from 67 W to 163 W across the 290 seconds you were pedalling and never once left Zone 1 (118-165 W), so the warm-up was ridden exactly as written. Cadence climbed 72 to 87 and settled there. Heart rate came up from 86 to about 125 by minute two, then sat flat between 124 and 128 for the last three minutes while power kept climbing another fifteen watts. Flat heart rate under rising power is the comfortable version of a warm-up, not a struggling one.

The stop itself is the informative part. The last pedal stroke is at 163 W — two watts under the Zone 1 ceiling and about ten seconds short of where the 130 minutes of Zone 2 would have begun. That is the shape of a decision rather than a fade: nothing in the trace is running away, nothing is sagging, and there was no rep to have failed.

So there is no Zone 2 body and no fast finish to analyse. The finish was already off the sheet this morning, which means what is actually missing is the 130 easy minutes and the reference block. The ramp did touch 163 W, essentially the block's own wattage, but the block is ten flat minutes sitting at minutes 20-30 and the extractor discards the first fifteen minutes of any ride — so nothing was collected, and this week's 165 W observation does not exist.

One honest limit on all of the above: the file was fetched at 18:30. If you went back out after that, tonight cannot see it.

1) ADAPT: CFF16 CLASSIFIED FAILED, ABSORBED, NOT OWED. Started and aborted at 5:09 — load 3 against a planned 131, compliance zero, planned event 131228735 left unpaired, and the 05:20 hygiene pass clears it overnight. Rule applied: lost easy volume is absorbed rather than chased, reinforced by the deload rule that nothing is ever added back. There is also nowhere honest to put it — tomorrow is the run retest and Monday opens week 13. expected.rides goes 3 to 2, the week closes at 2 rides and 1 run, and RT19 is untouched. What is genuinely lost is the reference block, and that is now a second straight week in which the 165 W series has not moved.

2) I AM NOT GOING TO NAME A CAUSE, BECAUSE THE FILE CANNOT SEPARATE THEM. Two candidates fit. One is plain circumstance — the stop lands cleanly on the warm-up boundary with a heart rate of 128 and a smooth ramp behind it, which is what stepping off a bike looks like rather than what failing on one looks like. The other is the morning: the readiness index was the lowest on the twenty-one-day board and the plan's own second cut had already been taken before you clipped in. Both are plausible, the trace favours neither, and neither becomes a rule or carries past tonight. If it was simply the day, that is a perfectly good answer — I would just rather have it from you in a note than infer it.

3) THE RETEST IS NOW CLEANER THAN THE PLAN EXPECTED, AND THAT IS A REAL UPSIDE. Sunday's plan carried an explicit caveat: RT19 follows a 150-minute ride, so if the block came in soft that was a live alternative explanation to threshold down, and tune.py would have had to argue with it before moving an anchor. That caveat is now void. Tomorrow's block lands on legs that did five minutes of Zone 1 and a load of 3 — the freshest run retest available anywhere in this week, by a distance. Whatever else today was, it bought you a clean measurement.

4) TWO OF FIVE ENDURANCE SESSIONS ARE GONE THIS WEEK AND I AM NAMING IT WITHOUT ACTING ON IT. RAn3 Thursday, CFF16 today. The standing guard for a second failure inside one week is to convert the remaining hard endurance to easy, and I am deliberately not applying it: RT19 is the block-boundary retest, and watering down a tune block is the worst outcome available — full fatigue, a number produced anyway, and that number then prescribing nine weeks. The plan's answer for a flat Sunday is to MOVE it into Monday, not to soften it, and that is the down-branch below. Meanwhile the guard's actual intent — an easy day sitting in front of the next hard one — is precisely what today turned into.

Legs heavy, or the block's pace only available by pushing? Move the retest into Monday of week 13 rather than watering it down. That is the plan's own written instruction and it is the better of the two errors by a long way — a half-executed tune block costs the full fatigue and still produces a number that would set nine weeks of zones. Both are a good day's work; one of them is a decision rather than a session.

And if it runs outdoors on rolling ground, the pace and heart-rate scatter that produces is terrain, not an execution fault. Run the effort, not the watch.

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

This is the same session that set FTP 236 on 28 July, so the comparison is direct and like-for-like.
Set the effort in the first 3–4 minutes and then stop adjusting. One early correction, never a stair-step. tune.py reads steadiness as a coefficient of variation, and a sawtooth block reads as a dirty measurement even when the average is right.
Target the band and let heart rate tell the story. Last time the block averaged 229.5 W with the plateau at 158.5 against a bike LTHR of 159 — that is what a clean one looks like.
Do not ride it as a test of how much you can hurt. A block you fade out of measures your pacing, not your threshold. If heart rate is clearly under 159 at 24 minutes you have left something on the table — and that is the better of the two errors.
If today arrives genuinely flat, MOVE the retest to Thursday and drop RAn3. Do not water it down. A half-executed tune block costs full fatigue, produces a number anyway, and that number then sets nine weeks of zones.
